verses.text: All the people gathered together as one in the open square in front of the Water Gate. They asked Ezra the teacher to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the LORD had given to Israel.
So on the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the law out to the crowd of men and women and everyone old enough to understand.

He read it aloud from early morning until noon, as he faced the square in front of the Water Gate. He read to the men, the women, and all who could understand, and all the people listened carefully to the book of the law.

Ezra the teacher stood on a high wooden platform built for this purpose. Beside him on his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah. On his left stood Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Ezra opened the book where all the people could see him, because he was standing above them. As he opened it, all the people stood up.
Ezra praised the LORD, the great God, and all the people lifted their hands and answered, "Amen! Amen!" Then they bowed down and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.

The Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah helped the people understand the law while the people stood in their places.
They read from the book of God's law clearly and explained what it meant, so the people understood what was being read.

Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who were teaching the people said to them all, "This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not be sad or cry." They said this because all the people had been crying as they listened to the words of the law.

Nehemiah said, "Go and enjoy good food and sweet drinks. Send some to people who have nothing ready, because this day is holy to our Lord. Do not be sad, because the joy of the LORD is your strength."
The Levites calmed all the people, saying, "Be quiet, because this is a holy day. Do not be sad."
Then all the people went away to eat and drink, to send food to others, and to celebrate with great joy, because they now understood the words that had been explained to them.
On the second day, the family leaders of all the people, along with the priests and Levites, gathered around Ezra the teacher to study the words of the law.
They found written in the law, which the LORD had given through Moses, that the Israelites were to live in shelters during the festival of the seventh month.

It also said they should announce this in all their towns and in Jerusalem: "Go out to the hills and bring back branches from olive trees, wild olive trees, myrtles, palms, and other leafy trees, to make shelters, as it is written."

So the people went out and brought back branches and made shelters for themselves. They built them on their roofs, in their courtyards, in the courtyards of God's temple, in the square by the Water Gate, and in the square by the Ephraim Gate.
Everyone who had come back from being prisoners built shelters and lived in them. The Israelites had not done this since the days of Joshua son of Nun. Everyone was full of joy.
Every day, from the first day to the last, Ezra read from the book of God's law. They celebrated the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day they held a special gathering, as the law requires.
